"What exists, on the contrary, is an orchestrated campaign against our government." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, responding to Javier Milei Milei accused Mexico and Brazil of financing an "anti-Argentina" campaign during the 2026 World Cup. Sheinbaum: false. Mexico doesn't meddle in other countries' affairs — and asks for the same.

🇲🇽🌎 "Democracy, democracy, democracy. Power of the people, government of the people." "It's the self-determination of peoples — whatever the people of Nicaragua decides. We always stand with democracy, in all its terms." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on Nicaragua Asked about Daniel Ortega's announcement that there will be no more elections in Nicaragua, Sheinbaum defended self-determination. Would she apply the same in Mexico? "Here we even have recall referendums. Elections every six years."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>US TO MEXICO: BUILD OUR TARIFF WALL AGAINST CHINA</u>

Washington asked Mexico to replicate its Section 232 wall — 50% tariffs on Chinese steel and aluminum — as the price of keeping preferential treatment for North American steel, four sources familiar with the talks told El Financiero.

US steelmakers also demand a "melted and poured" rule — steel forged in North America, not just finished here — and want to raise required regional steel content in cars from 70% to 85%.

Mexico already slashed Chinese steel purchases and tariffed some 1,500 products this year. The US wants a framework deal before year-end; the next round lands in Washington in September.

🇲🇽🥇 <u>MEXICO FRONT AND CENTER AT THE CENTROAMERICAN GAMES</u>

Santo Domingo hosts the centenary edition of the Central American and Caribbean Games — and Mexico led the opening parade, honored for organizing the very first edition back in 1926.

The tricolor delegation is the largest in the Games' history: 646 athletes defending the titles won in Barranquilla 2018 and San Salvador 2023, aiming past the 353 medals of the last edition. Mexico holds the all-time record with 4,200 medals.

A century later, still the reference.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>ISSSTE TAKES FREE SPECIALIZED SURGERY TO FRESNILLO</u>

First surgical day in traumatology and orthopedics at the ISSSTE's "Fresnillo" hospital in Zacatecas: 76 patients benefited in the opening stretch.

"On Tuesdays, Thursdays and weekends our surgeons treated knee, hip and rotator-cuff injuries and other problems," the institute reported.

Public health that reaches where the private system never bothered to go.

🇲🇽📉 <u>CDMX: HIGH-IMPACT CRIME DOWN 64% SINCE 2019</u>

Clara Brugada reported it at the interstate security summit: high-impact crimes in Mexico City have fallen 64% compared to 2019, and June 2026 was the capital's lowest-homicide June since 2015 — achieved in the middle of a World Cup.

Vehicle theft dropped 40%, from 18 cars a day to 14. "Homicides and vehicle theft, with and without violence, have been coming down," she said.

Seven years, one security model, and numbers that keep falling.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S JUDGES RESURRECT DEAD PATENTS FOR BIG PHARMA</u>

The patents expired. Mexican judges brought them back to life.

Courts have blocked the production of generics of three drugs after transnational labs shielded themselves with amparos under the old NAFTA — the same trick that let Amgen "revive" its Denosumab patent (expired in 2022, stretched to 2027) even though two Mexican firms already sell the biosimilar at half the price.

Anafam director Ricardo del Olmo calls the rulings "a grave legal and institutional setback" that "violates the people's right to health".

This is the judiciary Mexicans voted to reform.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MILEI INVENTS A PLOT, MEXICO ANSWERS WITH FACTS</u>

Javier Milei claimed — without presenting a single piece of evidence — that Mexico, Brazil and the US Democratic Party finance an "anti-Argentina campaign".

President Sheinbaum from Palacio Nacional: "It is false. There is no campaign against any country in the world, nor against any government. What there IS is an orchestrated campaign against our government, but we do not meddle in other countries. Self-determination of the peoples — and we ask for the same: respect."

The far right exports accusations. Mexico answers with international law.
